title: ARC-000: Ultrasonic Sonar Scanner
summary: I built a servo-swept ultrasonic scanner with an Arduino and 3D-printed mounting hardware, then worked through why its scans did not match the real scene.
result: Traced false readings to off-axis echoes in the sensor's beam cone, which led directly to the ARC-001 sensor study.
spec: The scanner reported distances clustered within 0.3 cm of each other even when the objects in front of it were at different ranges.
I isolated variables in sequence: tape-measure checks, higher-resolution readings, 5-ping averaging, and a minimal open-space test.
I traced the fault to off-axis echoes within the sensor's ±15° beam cone and designed printed shrouds in multiple lengths to trade interference rejection against signal strength.
Arduino (C++), NewPing, HC-SR04, SG90 servo, Python, Processing, SolidWorks, Bambu FDM
